AC5 detail (kept out of the description to stay under the 8000-char review-admission limit).

The one existing assertion this change deliberately updates is in test_strict_terminal_push_classes_have_distinct_reasons_and_preserve_state.

Before: the strict path was SILENT on stdout/stderr, because _raise_if_strict raises BEFORE the terminal logger.warning, so a strict caller got the exception and nothing else.

After: a transport fault RETRIES first, and each retry announces itself before we know the attempt will end terminally. That notice is the only in-run signal that delivery is degraded, so silence is no longer the contract for the transport class. The policy-decline class still asserts exact silence (one attempt, no output).

The retry count is asserted on caplog rather than capsys because handler configuration decides whether the notice also reaches the captured streams: locally it lands in the log capture, on CI it reached the captured streams. caplog is deterministic in both.
